description: Same great education, exciting new location for 2026 - Join us this fall in one of San Francisco's most distinctive neighborhoods at the beautifully reimagined Hotel Kabuki! Join us for an engaging and practical OBGYN CME conference designed to keep clinicians at the forefront of Reproductive healthcare. This program will highlight the latest evidence and clinical updates across a range of important topics, including complex contraception, gynecologic surgery, cancer prevention, and menopausal care. Expert faculty will share insights on managing both common and complex conditions in obstetrics and gynecology, with a focus on translating new data into everyday clinical practice. Through concise, evidence-based lectures, participants will gain practical strategies for improving patient care across the reproductive lifespan. Attendees will leave with actionable tools to enhance surgical decision-making, strengthen patient counseling, and implement clinical protocols that improve outcomes for diverse patient populations. Whether you are looking to refine your approach to chronic conditions in pregnancy, stay current on updates in reproductive health, or incorporate new guidelines into practice, this conference will provide the knowledge and confidence to elevate your everyday care. Onsite and Remote Learning Options: The course will be offered as a live conference. Registrants have the option to attend in person or to tune in remotely via zoom live stream during programming hours (Pacific Time). Login instructions along with the digital syllabus will be shared with attendees before the meeting. Included in your registration fee is access to the course recordings on demand after the conference and for 30 days after the course. You must tune in to the live conference (in person or remotely) to claim CME. Registration Fees - Early Bird Pricing in effect until 9/5/2026: Physicians: $825 / $875Nurses/APPs/Other Health Care Professionals: $675 / $725Residents/Trainees/Fellows: $525 / $575For more information and to register, please visit: https://ucsf.cloud-cme.com/obgyn2026

description: Exercise can improve physical functioning in cancer patients. It can reduce the feelings of fatigue, depression, nausea and weakness that can arise during and after cancer treatment. The UCSF Core and More class includes Pilates-based mat exercises to work on core strength and stability. We use rollers, bands and body weight as tools to enhance range of motion, flexibility, balance and muscular strength. Our goal is for you to have fun and increase your ability to perform daily activities. This class is sponsored by the UCSF Cancer Resource Center. It is open to current UCSF cancer patients and survivors. Registration is required for this class. To participate, you must undergo a pre-screening with an exercise counselor. For more information, call (415) 502-5547. There may be a waitlist for this course.

description: IHPS Health Policy Grand Rounds The Medicare Hospice Benefit provides interdisciplinary end-of-life care to millions of Americans, but its eligibility, payment, and regulatory structures were developed in a different era and often fit poorly with the long and unpredictable course of dementia. Drs. Lauren Hunt and Krista Harrison will draw on their complementary research programs, combining population-level quantitative evidence with qualitative perspectives from bereaved caregivers and hospice professionals, to examine how hospice policy and organizational incentives shape access, care delivery, disenrollment, disparities, and family experiences. The findings highlight tensions between expanding access to needed care and preventing undertreatment, inappropriate enrollment, and profiteering. Hospice policy must be redesigned to better fit the needs of people with dementia and their families while preserving the benefits of hospice care.

description: Join us for our Stem Cell Genome Engineering Series | Organoid Models, which highlights advances in genome engineering for stem cell biology and therapeutic development, aligning with our vision to Discover, Engineer, Heal. At our Nov 10 session, we will hear from speaker Michelle Gbenedio, who will present "Patient-Derived Organoid Resources: From 3D Model Development to Disease Modeling and Drug Screening." Advances in organoid technology have offered new opportunities for studying human biology and disease in vitro. In collaboration with UCSF clinicians, the Organoid Core has established a living organoid biobank of over 100 organoid lines to serve as a platform for collaborative research at UCSF. The talk will cover how these 3D models are generated and used for downstream applications like genomic and biomarker analyses as well as testing therapeutic responses. Speaker Lineup | Fall 2026 Oct 13 | Dan Wagner | Single-Cell Genomics: From Cell Atlases to Genotype-Resolved Biology Oct 27 | James Gardner | Normothermic perfusion systems as platforms for groundbreaking ex vivo human biology Nov 10 | Michelle Gbenedio | Getting started with organoids Dec 8 | Alex Pollen | Experimental and analytical techniques for village culture organoids UCSF welcomes all participants to our events.
